content.title: About
content.content: Skinless chicken meat grilled without added sauce is a lean source of protein. It is rich in B‑vitamins, minerals (iron, zinc, phosphorus) and contains very little fat when no oil is used during cooking.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken is the most widely consumed poultry worldwide, featured in virtually every cuisine.
Grilling imparts a characteristic smoky flavor through Maillard reactions while leaving the natural taste intact without sauce.
Skinless grilled chicken breast provides about 31 g of protein and less than 3 g of fat per 100 g.
Chicken is a good source of collagen, which turns into gelatin during cooking and supports joint health.
Proper grilling preserves most vitamins compared with deep‑frying, which can cause greater nutrient loss.

items.title: High protein content
items.content: Protein is essential for tissue growth and repair, supports the immune system and promotes satiety.

items.title: Low fat
items.content: Absence of skin and sauce makes the dish suitable for low‑fat and calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: B3 (niacin) and B6 play key roles in energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Chicken provides iron, zinc and phosphorus, important for blood formation, immunity and bone health.

items.title: Supports muscle mass
items.content: A complete amino‑acid profile helps maintain and build muscle, especially for active individuals.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Insufficient cooking may leave harmful bacteria such as Salmonella or Campylobacter alive.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: A small number of people can develop allergic reactions to chicken proteins.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: If the meat was previously marinated, sodium levels can be high; plain grilling without added salt is preferable.

items.title: Formation of carcinogens
items.content: Excessive charring on the grill can produce heterocyclic amines; aim for a golden brown crust rather than black char.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Skinless grilled chicken can be served as a main dish, sliced into salads, added to soups, wraps, or used as a sandwich filling. It pairs well with vegetables, lemon, herbs and light yogurt‑based sauces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep raw chicken refrigerated at ≤ 4 °C for no more than 2 days, and cooked meat in an airtight container for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze in a sealed bag at ‑18 °C; thaw in the refrigerator before use.

content.title: About
content.content: Whipped topping is a ready‑to‑use aerated dessert product made from cream, sugar and stabilizers. It has a light, airy texture, a gentle buttery flavor and is used to garnish and enrich desserts, drinks and baked goods.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Whipped topping is often sold in aerosol cans, which makes dispensing convenient.
The formulation may contain vegetable oils, providing greater stability during storage.
In some countries the product is fortified with vitamins A and D.
Its texture is achieved by injecting air under pressure, increasing the volume 5–7 times.
Whipped topping can be sweetened or neutral, allowing use in a variety of culinary applications.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Cream, like other dairy products, provides calcium essential for bone and teeth health.

items.title: Vitamin D
items.content: Some versions are fortified with vitamin D, which supports the immune system and calcium absorption.

items.title: Low carbohydrate content
items.content: Whipped topping typically contains modest amounts of sugar, making it suitable for moderate consumption in low‑carb diets.

items.title: Enhances flavor
items.content: Adding whipped topping can boost taste perception without the need for large amounts of heavy cream.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: The product contains dairy proteins and may trigger allergic reactions in individuals with lactose intolerance or milk allergy.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Whipped topping is rich in fats, so it should be consumed in moderation, especially when managing weight.

items.title: Stabilizer content
items.content: Certain stabilizers (e.g., emulsifiers) may cause discomfort in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Pressurized storage
items.content: Aerosol cans require careful handling; a damaged can can pose a safety hazard.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Whipped topping can be added to desserts, cakes, ice cream, coffee, hot chocolate, and used to decorate fruit and pastries. It can be lightly whipped with a spoon for a firmer texture.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the can in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, use the product within 2–3 days. Do not store at temperatures above 25°C.
